fit.gap_handling_summary: The documents accurately position an early-career frontend developer with academic full-stack experience rather than manufacturing professional backend tenure. Accessibility, Next.js, testing and teaching experience are well selected. The major experience shortfall remains, while end-to-end testing, OWASP, GDPR, NestJS and production health-data handling are not demonstrated; the letter could explain the junior-level transfer more directly without claiming missing experience.

artefacts: The PDF extraction merges the institution and date: "Liffey Institute of Technology2021–2025".
issues: The Spring 2025 teaching-assistant role appears after the May–August 2024 internship rather than in reverse chronological order.
Projects occupy most of the first page while the relevant internship starts on page two.
The gallery and yoga-site descriptions are repeated across Projects and Professional Experience, consuming space that could support a more balanced two-page layout.
The teaching-assistant entry does not identify an institution or employer; this should be clarified from the candidate rather than guessed.

reasons: The text extracts in a sensible order, with standard headings and intact technical terminology apart from the institution/date join.
Core React, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL, Jest, Next.js and Storybook terms are present.
Firebase Authentication and public API consumption provide relevant authentication and third-party-integration matches.
The required two years of professional React/TypeScript experience is not supported; academic projects and part-time freelance work do not close that gap.
Several security, privacy and end-to-end-testing requirements are absent, appropriately avoiding unsupported keyword insertion.

issues: The third paragraph repeats Tidewatch and the yoga booking site shortly after they have already been introduced.
The long third paragraph becomes a catalogue of projects and tools rather than a focused argument for the candidate's contribution.
The letter does not clearly explain the transition from junior frontend experience to a role requesting two years of professional full-stack-related experience.
The closing emphasis on native English is accurate but less persuasive than a concise closing focused on the strongest relevant evidence.
Company tailoring is primarily through the principles and general accessibility mission; it does not engage with a specific Verdane product or patient workflow.
strengths: Names the correct company, role and Patient Experience team.
Uses concrete, supported accessibility outcomes and relevant backend project details.
Connects the yoga-studio work to the wellness domain without claiming regulated healthcare experience.
Uses the company's actual principles rather than invented cultural claims.
Avoids the earlier letter's stale student and internship-application framing.

culture_used: Making software useful and easy to use for the people it serves

overflow_or_cutoff: On CV page two, the long education heading runs into the right-aligned 2021–2025 date; the institution and date visibly touch and extract as "Technology2021–2025".
spacing_issues: The CV is visually unbalanced: page one is dense while page two is only 40.7% filled.
Professional Experience begins near the bottom of page one and continues on page two without a repeated section heading.
The cover letter's third paragraph is a comparatively dense block.
issues: The automated measurements report no problems, but the page image and extracted text reveal insufficient separation between the education institution and date.
Reducing repeated project descriptions would improve page balance and give professional experience greater prominence.

fluency_and_tone_issues: "hands-on experience building React and TypeScript applications, including Node.js/Express APIs" is slightly imprecise: the APIs are backend components of the applications, not React applications themselves.

"project work including a wellness booking site and Tidewatch" followed by "I have also built a Next.js booking site for a local yoga studio" repeats the same booking project as though introducing an additional example.
"I would bring" is repeated in the same long paragraph, making the letter sound formulaic.

notes_facts_used: Teaching assistant for a first-year web development lab in Spring 2025.
Supported approximately 30 students over one semester.
The distinction between project-only backend experience and professional frontend experience is preserved.
notes_facts_ignored: Second-place student hackathon result, three-person team, 24-hour delivery and frontend contribution.

parsed.summary: Both documents are factually grounded and make good use of the candidate's accessibility work, Next.js freelance project and academic Node.js/PostgreSQL experience. They do not invent professional backend experience, missing technologies or work-arrangement commitments, but the candidate still falls short of the required professional tenure. The main presentation weaknesses are duplicated project material, incorrect experience ordering, an unbalanced CV and a visible education/date collision. The cover letter is relevant and credible, but would benefit from less repetition and a sharper explanation of the candidate's junior-level contribution.
